picks.title: A Buddhist Monk on Why Life Feels Pointless – But Isn’t!
picks.summary: In today’s episode, Gen Rabten explores one of the biggest questions we can ask about our lives: what is the point? He explains how modern life can leave us feeling increasingly purposeless, whether through anxiety about the future, the pressure to achieve success, changing ideas about work and wealth, or the realization that the things we thought would make us happy often fail to provide lasting fulfilment. picks.reason: Addresses life's meaning and purpose through Buddha's teachings and modern issues.

picks.summary:
October 2001. James Low teaches on "The Integration of Stillness and Movement: the approach of different buddhist paths" at Kamalashila Institute in the Eifel region of Germany.

"Most of us who have been involved with buddhism for some time will have reflected a lot on impermanence, but it is never something to treat lightly. It is the royal road to an understanding of stillness and movement." ~ James Low

picks.title: Meditation: Resting in Reality (24 min)
picks.summary: In this guided meditation, Tara Brach invites us to relax out of the thinking mind and return to the living presence of the moment. Through a gentle body scan, awareness of breath, sound and sensation, we begin to sense the aliveness that is always here—and to rest more fully in reality. As the mind naturally wanders into thought, we practice letting go and opening again to the changing river of experience. picks.reason: Tara Brach guides a meditation resting in present reality, a direct Buddhist practice.

picks.title: Pathways to Trusting the Gold
picks.summary: What would it mean to truly trust the goodness that lives within you? In this talk, Tara Brach explores what she calls "trusting the gold"—awakening from the stories of deficiency, fear and separation that keep us from recognizing our deepest nature. We may spend much of our lives trying to improve ourselves, earn approval or finally become "enough," while overlooking the loving awareness that is already here. Tara explores how our early experiences of nurturing and belonging shape our capacity to trust ourselves, and how mindfulness and compassion can help heal the places that feel unworthy,
picks.reason: Tara Brach explores trusting innate goodness beyond fear and deficiency, a Buddhist insight.

picks.title: Ordinary Mind is the Way
picks.summary:
In this Wednesday night Dharma talk, Sensei Koshin Flint Sparks explores a simple and radical teaching: our ordinary experience is itself the awakened way. By ordinary, he means not our passing thoughts but the unmanipulated mind that holds them. Many of us come to practice believing that awakening lies somewhere else, in a later time, a better state, or in exceptional people unlike ourselves.
Source
picks.reason: Sensei Koshin Sparks teaches that ordinary mind is the awakened way, a core Zen Buddhist insight.
